newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on weather concerns.

text.p: Worries that cool temperatures in the U.S. Midwest will hinder growth of the newly planted corn crop helped push corn prices to a higher close Friday, traders said.

Some forecasts for next week have temperatures staying unseasonably cool in much of the Midwest and also indicate rain. Low temperatures in Ohio and eastern Illinois are seen dipping to the mid 30s (degrees Fahrenheit) on Friday and Saturday, meteorologists said.
While those temperatures are not low enough to cause freeze damage, they could hinder development, analysts said.
Rain also slowed planting efforts Friday in the western Corn Belt, analysts and traders said.
"The corn market has been supported by the fact that fieldwork has pretty much come to a halt out here," said Jason Roose, grain analyst with U.S. Commodities in West Des Moines, Iowa.
Roose also said that much of the corn that was planted early had not yet emerged because soil temperatures were still low.
CBOT corn futures ended three to four cents per bushel higher, with July up 3-1/2 at $2.88 per bushel.
On Monday, traders are looking for the U.S. Department of Agriculture to show the corn crop 67 to 75 percent planted in the crop progress report.
USDA will also release supply and demand forecasts on Monday, but analysts and traders were looking for the government to make only a few adjustments to corn forecasts.
On the day, Iowa Grain bought two million bushels December, Continental Grain bought 1.5 million July and Cargill bought one million July. Merrill Lynch sold two million bushels July.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 1,500 July $3.00 calls and Continental Grain bought 1,000 December $2.80 calls and sold 1,000 December $3.40 calls, pit sources said..
Volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts. That figure is lower than Thursday's final volume of 64,713 contracts, according to CBOT data.
